title: Prenatal exposure to arsenic and cadmium impacts infectious disease-related genes within the glucocorticoid receptor signal transduction pathway.
ehr_evidence: Twelve datasets were gathered from previous human cohort studies evaluating mRNA changes, DNA methylation changes, or protein expression changes associated with prenatal exposure to iAs or Cd.
summary: A comparative genomic enrichment analysis integrating twelve human pregnancy cohort datasets to identify genes and pathways linking prenatal arsenic and cadmium exposure to infectious disease susceptibility.
key_findings: 82 infection and exposure-related (IER) genes were identified that overlap between infectious disease signaling and prenatal iAs/Cd exposure.
19 of 82 IER genes were enriched for the glucocorticoid receptor signal transduction pathway (p = 1.58 × 10−18).
9 of 82 IER genes were present in the TNFR1 pathway (p = 5.01 × 10−13).
8 of 82 IER genes were present in the toll-like receptor pathway (p = 6.31 × 10−13).
61% (50/82) of IER genes were shown to be modulated by iAs and 41% (34/82) by Cd in the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database.
data_source_type: published genomic, epigenomic, and proteomic datasets from human pregnancy cohorts
population: pregnant women and newborns/infants from cohorts in Bangladesh, Thailand, Mexico, and the United States
exposure_domain: prenatal and early-life exposure to inorganic arsenic and cadmium
limitations: genomic and epigenomic endpoints can be transient
original studies had small sample sizes
incomplete analysis of confounders in source studies
variations in exposure duration and demographics across cohorts
reliance on published gene lists rather than raw data
CTD validation included in vitro and animal model data
